game_concept: A action defense set in Mt. Pyre – Vent Garden, a garden growing near vents: the fire warden must handle smoke serpents while practicing data types & operators. Core idea – Modulo Gate: Use % to decide which gates in Vent Garden open (even, odd, divisible by 3).
theme: Mt. Pyre – Vent Garden: a garden growing near vents
core_gameplay_loop: Inspect the circuit board, solve the CP1 station, and advance the signal through its gates.
secondary_mechanics: Hint tokens that reveal one line of code
player_objective: Read a rectangle's width and height. Calculate its area and display the result. Problem values 21, 5; test inputs [{'width': 15, 'height': 5}, {'width': 10, 'height': 6}, {'width': 20, 'height': 7}, {'width': 21, 'height': 21}, {'width': 21, 'height': 5}].
controls: Drag flowchart symbols onto numbered positions and follow the arrows. Check chart executes every case. Arrow keys and Enter also place selected blocks.
win_condition: Construct a complete chart that passes every executable input/output case.
lose_condition: The available unsuccessful chart checks are exhausted.
assets_style: Shared Kenney CC0 tile and audio assets with deterministic Canvas layouts; assets are not duplicated per game.
duplicate_check_notes: Unique combination of primary mechanic 'Modulo Gate' (Week 2 slot 3), mission type 'Survival Siege', and setting 'Vent Garden'. No other file shares this combination; games sharing the mechanic differ in mission/win condition and setting, and games sharing the setting use a different mechanic.

region.name: Mt. Pyre
region.mood: low war drums, rumbling bass and crackling fire effects

tutorial: Use terminator, input/output, process and decision symbols.
Test the chart with every example input.
source_player_objective: Protect the ash barrier from smoke serpents in Vent Garden: keep the gates_open meter above zero by applying the concept correctly until the 50-second timer ends.
source_lose_condition: gates_open drops to 0, or lives reach 0, before the 50-second timer ends.
hint: Trace the arrows. Read input before using it; use rectangles for assignments and diamonds for decisions.
